pr_title: Bluetooth: Audio: Add support for using bidirectional CIS for Audio Streams
pr_body:
This PR adds support for using a bidirectional CIS for a IN and OUT audio stream. The stack will couple streams together automatically, and will always attempt to use the least amount of CIS. 

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/41193
pr_comments: To fix https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45374 the allocation of ISO channels (from bt_unicast_client_new_audio_iso), needs to be done when creating the group or when added streams to the group, otherwise we can't create the CIG without all streams being configured first.

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Couple `IN` audio stream with an `OUT` audio stream
issue_context.body:
A CIS can be bi-dirctional, but an audio stream is not.  We want to be able to use the same CIS for both an IN stream and an OUT stream.

An audio stream is always either IN or OUT, but a client may setup a single bidirectional CIS for both an IN and an OUT audio stream. We will need some way of coupling such streams.

E.g.
- a function to pair two streams, giving them a reference to each other
- currently: audio streams have a CIS, change to having a reference to a CIS



Depends on https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/41194

review_comments: Do you plan to add LC3 encoder as well?

That is probably a good idea, but the change in this sample was mostly to be able to test the stack change. The LC3 support should be added in a separate PR: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45595
Why the ISO is not a member of `bt_ascs_ase`?

That is also an option. The reason why it isn't, is that two ASE may use the same CIS and thus the same `struct bt_audio_iso`. In other words, there isn't a 1:1 between ASE and `struct bt_audio_iso`, and `struct bt_audio_iso isos[ASE_COUNT];` may also in the future to be less than `ASE_COUNT` (e.g. if we want to support fewer started streams than ASEs).
Indeed. One ASE can be assigned to only one CIS, but one CIS can be assigned to multiple ASE's. Thus it's intuitive that each ASE keeps assigned CIS

Not sure I follow your comment. 

If we move the ISO into the `bt_ascs_ase` then we cannot have 2 ASEs with the same ISO.
Now I see it. I thought it's pointer rather than value. Sorry :)

`CONFIG_BT_AUDIO_UNICAST_CLIENT_ASE_SNK_COUNT` is correct, as `SINK` refers to remote sinks. 

This is actually something that has been bothering me a little:

Should "sink" refer to a local sink (i.e. remote source ASE), or a remote sink ASE?
Ah, OK, I understand now. I do not have opinion regarding that, but I can see this might be a bit confusing for the user
